author: c2-sql-edu-critic (independent education critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; rechecked commit 02be5a14)

findings.claim: New at 02be5a14, D7 and §12 (retention, not recognition). The restored bank shortens distractors, so the correct option is now clearly the longest in "o2 why not WHERE" (65 characters against at most 35) and "o3 fix the ungrouped column" (64 against 26). A learner can score by picking the longest option without recalling the rule. DESIGN.md "Assessment: options, confidence, feedback" requires comparable option lengths.
findings.recommendation: Rebalance the option lengths with authoring/tools/gift/answer-order.mjs: lengthen distractors or trim the correct options, keeping every option's meaning. authoring/tests/gift-answer-order.test.mjs freezes each item's semantics against a baseline. If that test also blocks wording-only length changes, the captain or tooling owner must decide whether to refresh the baseline after review. Do not leave the cue in place.

items.note: Activity 2 is now a typed fix: students-by-city.sql starts with SELECT city, name, COUNT(*) FROM students GROUP BY city;. Running it unchanged gets "That is still the starting query, which stops with an ERROR because name is neither grouped nor inside an aggregate", and the intended fix passes.
The hints now ask reasoning questions ("Decide what each output row stands for…", "Which clause filters groups?") instead of spelling the clauses.

Open as originally written. "o3 fix the ungrouped column" still uses DISTINCT, which is never taught, and MIN(name) on text.
